key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the prosecution's circumstantial evidence, including the last seen theory, but found it insufficient to establish guilt due to lack of corroboration and inconsistencies in witness statements.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW-4 and PW-5) as inimical to the appellant due to their civil suit and personal conflicts, thus their statements could not be readily relied upon without corroboration.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: January 3, 2004; Trial judgment: January 13, 2006; High Court decision: March 25, 2008; Supreme Court decision: July 30, 2019
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Shaurya Sahay, Amit Kumar, Advs.; Counsel for the State: Raj Singh Rana, Pankaj Kumar Singh, Sanjeet Paliwal, Avisek Minj, Vishwa Pal Singh, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR lodged, DNA test conducted, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted; High Court: Dismissed appeal; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, acquitted
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased and the appellant were familiar with each other and had planned to visit a village together. The body of the deceased was found burning in a 'Bitora', and DNA tests confirmed it was the deceased. Witnesses PW-4 and PW-5 claimed to have seen the appellant with the deceased and her children, and the appellant was convicted for murder.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's evidence was weak and full of contradictions. The witnesses PW-4 and PW-5 were inimical to the appellant as they had filed a suit for claiming the estate of Baburam, and their statements lacked corroboration. The evidence of last seen was deemed insufficient to sustain a conviction.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that circumstantial evidence must form a complete and unbroken chain of circumstances pointing to the guilt of the accused, and that the prosecution must prove all the circumstances connecting the accused to the crime.
precedent_relied_upon: Satpal v. State of Haryana (2018) 6 SCC 610; Asar Mohammad v. State of U.P. 2018 SCC OnLine SC 2179
other_sentence_order: The appellant was acquitted of the charges levelled against her. The bail bonds shall stand discharged. She is set at liberty, if not wanted in any other case.
